translations.idiomatic: Heaven still favored Wei and would provide a sovereign. The enthronement of a legitimate ruler was no deed of Huan's.

sentences.zh: 而歡阻兵安忍，自以為功。

translations.literal: Yet Huan, relying on his army and cruelly indulgent, took the credit as his own achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Huan, armed and ruthless, claimed the triumph for himself.

sentences.zh: 廣布腹心，跨州連郡，端揆禁闥，莫非親黨。

translations.literal: He spread trusted men widely, spanning provinces and linking commanderies; chief ministers and palace gates—none were not his kin and partisans.
translations.idiomatic: He planted his creatures across provinces and linked commanderies; every post at court and gate fell to kin and clients.

sentences.zh: 皆行貪虐，窫窳生人。

translations.literal: All practiced greed and cruelty, grinding down the living.
translations.idiomatic: They plundered and tormented the people without restraint.

sentences.zh: 而舊將名臣，正人直士，橫生瘡痏，動掛網羅。

translations.literal: Yet old generals and famed ministers, upright men and straight scholars, sprouted sores of injury and at every move were snared in nets.
translations.idiomatic: Veteran commanders and honest ministers were hounded at every turn and caught in his nets.

sentences.zh: 故武衛將軍伊琳，清貞剛毅，禁旅攸屬；

translations.literal: Thus Military Guard General Yi Lin—pure, firm, and resolute—was one on whom the palace guard relied;
translations.idiomatic: Military Guard General Yi Lin, a man of clean integrity on whom the palace guard depended,

sentences.zh: 直閣將軍鮮于康仁，忠亮驍傑，爪牙斯在：歡收而戮之，曾无聞奏。

translations.literal: Direct Attendant General Xianyu Kangren, loyal, bright, fierce, and outstanding, was one whose claws and teeth stood there: Huan seized and executed them without ever reporting to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: and Direct Attendant General Xianyu Kangren, a loyal and formidable champion of the throne—Huan seized them both and killed them without a word to the court.

sentences.zh: 司空高乾，是其黨與，每相影響，謀危社稷。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Gao Gan was his partisan; they constantly influenced one another and plotted to endanger the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Gao Gan was his accomplice; together they schemed against the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 但以姦志未從，恐先洩漏，乃密白朝廷，使殺高乾，方哭對其弟，稱天子橫戮。

translations.literal: But because their treacherous design had not yet been carried out, fearing prior disclosure, he secretly reported to the court and had Gao Gan killed; only then did he weep before Gan's younger brother, calling it the Son of Heaven's arbitrary execution.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure before their plot ripened, he secretly denounced Gao Gan to the court and had him killed—then wept before Gan's brother and blamed the emperor for a capricious execution.

sentences.zh: 孫騰、任祥，歡之心膂，並使入居樞近，伺國間隙，知歡逆謀將發，相繼逃歸，歡益加撫待，亦無陳白。

translations.literal: Sun Teng and Ren Xiang, the sinews of Huan's heart, were both placed within the pivot of power to watch for gaps in the state. Learning that Huan's treason was about to break out, they fled home in succession; Huan only treated them more kindly and made no report.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng and Ren Xiang, his closest confidants, were posted near the throne to watch for weakness. When they saw his treason ripening they fled one after another—yet Huan sheltered them and never informed the court.

sentences.zh: 然歡入洛之始，本有姦謀。

translations.literal: Yet from the beginning when Huan entered Luoyang, he already had treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: From the day Huan entered Luoyang he had been plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 令親人蔡儁作牧河、濟，厚相恩贍，以為東道主人。

translations.literal: He had his kinsman Cai Jun made governor of the He and Ji region, richly bestowing favor and support, making him master of the eastern route.
translations.idiomatic: He installed his kinsman Cai Jun as governor of He and Ji, lavishing favor on him as custodian of the eastern approach.

sentences.zh: 故關西大都督、清水公賀拔岳，勳德隆重，興亡攸寄，歡好亂樂禍，深相忌毒，乃與侯莫陳悅陰圖陷害。

translations.literal: Thus the former Grand Governor of Guanxi, Duke of Qingshui Heba Yue—merit and virtue weighty, the rise and fall of the age entrusted to him—Huan, who loved disorder and delighted in calamity, deeply envied and hated him, and together with Houmochen Yue secretly plotted harm and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yue, former Grand Governor of Guanxi and Duke of Qingshui, whose merit upheld the realm, was marked for death. Huan, a lover of chaos, conspired with Houmochen Yue to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 幕府以受律專征，便卽討戮。

translations.literal: The headquarters, having received the mandate and sole command to campaign, at once executed punishment and slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: This headquarters, commissioned to punish traitors, has already struck down Yue.

sentences.zh: 歡知逆狀已露，稍懷旅距，遂遣蔡儁拒代，令竇泰佐之。

translations.literal: Huan knew his treason was exposed and gradually harbored resistance; he thereupon sent Cai Jun to resist replacement and ordered Dou Tai to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan, his guilt laid bare, turned defiant. He sent Cai Jun to hold the frontier and Dou Tai to support him.

sentences.zh: 又遣侯景等云向白馬，輔世珍等徑趣石濟，高隆之、疋婁昭等屯據壺關，韓軌之徒擁衆蒲阪。

translations.literal: He also sent Hou Jing and others, claiming to march on Baima; Fu Shizhen and others pressed straight on Shiji; Gao Longzhi, Pilou Zhao, and others garrisoned Huguan; and Han Gui and his kind massed troops at Puban.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Hou Jing toward Baima, Fu Shizhen on Shiji, Gao Longzhi and Pilou Zhao at Huguan, and Han Gui with a host at Puban.

sentences.zh: 於是上書天子，數論得失，訾毀乘輿，威侮朝廷。

translations.literal: Thereupon he addressed memorials to the Son of Heaven, repeatedly debating right and wrong, slandering the imperial carriage, and insulting the court with overbearing force.
translations.idiomatic: He bombarded the throne with memorials, reviling the emperor and browbeating the court.

sentences.zh: 藉此微庸，冀茲大寶。

translations.literal: Relying on these slight services, he hoped for the great treasure.
translations.idiomatic: On the strength of petty gains he reached for the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 溪壑可盈，禍心不測。

translations.literal: Gorges and ravines may be filled, yet the heart of calamity cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: His greed has no bottom; his malice no limit.

sentences.zh: 或言徑赴荊楚，開疆於外；

translations.literal: Some say he will go straight to Jing and Chu and open territory abroad;
translations.idiomatic: Some say he will march south into Jing and Chu to carve out new lands;

sentences.zh: 或言分詣伊洛，取彼讒人；

translations.literal: some say he will divide forces to Yi and Luo to take those slanderers;
translations.idiomatic: others that he will split his army toward Luoyang to seize his enemies at court;

sentences.zh: 或言欲來入關，與幕府決戰。

translations.literal: some say he wishes to come into the Pass and fight a decisive battle with the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: still others that he means to cross into the Pass and settle matters with this headquarters in battle.

sentences.zh: 今聖明御運，天下清夷，百寮師師，四隩來暨。

translations.literal: Now the sage and bright hold the turning of fortune; all under Heaven is clear and tranquil; the hundred offices are orderly; the four frontiers come to gather.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sage emperor holds the helm, the realm is at peace, the bureaucracy stands in order, and the four quarters pay homage.

sentences.zh: 人盡忠良，誰為君側？

translations.literal: Every man is loyal and good—who then is at the ruler's side?
translations.idiomatic: The court is full of loyal men—who, then, is the villain at the emperor's ear?

sentences.zh: 而歡威福自己，生是亂階，緝構南箕，指鹿為馬，包藏凶逆，伺我神器。

translations.literal: Yet Huan wields blessing and authority for himself, begetting the steps of disorder, weaving the net of the Southern Dipper, calling a deer a horse, concealing fierce treason, and watching for our sacred vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Huan makes himself the source of power, sows rebellion, twists truth into lies, hides treason, and covets the throne.

sentences.zh: 是而可忍，孰不可容！

translations.literal: If this can be borne, what cannot be tolerated!
translations.idiomatic: If this can be endured, nothing cannot!

sentences.zh: 幕府折沖宇宙，親當受脤，銳師百萬，彀騎千羣，裹糧坐甲，唯敵是俟，義之所在，糜軀匪恡。

translations.literal: The headquarters repels enemies across the cosmos, personally receiving the sacrificial flesh; sharp armies number in the millions, strong cavalry in thousands of squads; wrapped grain and seated armor, waiting only for the enemy; where righteousness lies, wasting the body without stinginess.
translations.idiomatic: This headquarters stands between heaven and earth with armies in the millions and cavalry by the thousand. Our men sit in armor with rations packed, waiting only for the foe—and where duty calls, they will spend themselves without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 況頻有詔書，班告天下，稱歡逆亂，徵兵致伐。

translations.literal: Moreover, edicts have repeatedly been issued, proclaimed to all under Heaven, calling Huan's treason and disorder and summoning troops to march against him.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial edicts have already gone out to the realm naming Huan a rebel and calling the hosts to war.

sentences.zh: 今便分命將帥，應機進討。

translations.literal: Now at once command will be divided among generals to advance and attack as opportunity allows.
translations.idiomatic: Generals will now be dispatched to strike wherever opportunity opens.

sentences.zh: 或趣其要害，或襲其窟宅，電繞蛇擊，霧合星羅。

translations.literal: Some will press their vital points, some raid their lairs; lightning coils and serpent strikes, mist gathers and stars array.
translations.idiomatic: Some columns will hit their vitals, others their strongholds—striking like lightning, closing like mist and stars.

sentences.zh: 而歡違負天地，毒被人鬼，乘此掃蕩，易同俯拾。

translations.literal: And Huan has betrayed Heaven and Earth; his poison reaches men and ghosts. Riding this sweep, taking him will be as easy as picking up what lies before one on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Huan has defied heaven and earth and poisoned men and spirits alike. At this sweep he will fall as easily as scooping what lies at one's feet.

sentences.zh: 歡若渡河，稍逼宗廟，則分命諸將，直取幷州，幕府躬自東轅，電赴伊洛；

translations.literal: If Huan crosses the river and gradually presses the ancestral temples, then command will be divided among the generals to take Bingzhou straight, and the headquarters will personally turn the eastern axle and fly to Yi and Luo;
translations.idiomatic: If he crosses the river toward the ancestral shrines, our generals will drive on Bingzhou while this headquarters races east to Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 若固其巢穴，未敢發動，亦命羣帥，百道俱前，轘裂賊臣，以謝天下。

translations.literal: if he holds fast in his nest and dares not stir, command will likewise be given to the host of commanders to advance on a hundred routes, crushing the rebel minister to answer to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: if he hides in his lair and dares not move, a hundred columns will advance together and tear the traitor apart to appease the realm.

sentences.zh: 其州鎮郡縣，率土人黎，或州鄉冠冕，或勳庸世濟，並宜捨逆歸順，立效軍門。

translations.literal: Provinces, commands, commanderies, and counties—the people of the land, whether local gentry of state and village or families whose merit served generations—should all abandon rebellion and return to loyalty, establishing merit at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: To every province, command, and county—to gentry and to families long in the emperor's service—we say: abandon the rebel, return to loyalty, and earn merit under our banners.

sentences.zh: 封賞之科，已有別格。

translations.literal: The statutes of enfeoffment and reward already have separate regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and enfeoffments are set forth in separate regulations.

sentences.zh: 凡百君子，可不勉歟。

translations.literal: All you gentlemen—can you not exert yourselves!
translations.idiomatic: Every loyal man among you—will you not do your utmost?

sentences.zh: 太祖謂諸將曰：「高歡雖智不足而詐有餘，今聲言欲西，其意在入洛。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke said to the generals, "Though Gao Huan's wisdom is insufficient, his deceit is more than enough. Now he declares he intends to go west; his real aim is to enter Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Duke told his officers, "Gao Huan lacks wisdom but not cunning. He talks of marching west; he means Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 吾欲令寇洛率馬步萬餘，自涇州東引；

translations.literal: I wish to have Kou Luo lead more than ten thousand horse and foot east from Jingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: I will send Kou Luo with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry east from Jingzhou;

sentences.zh: 王羆率甲士一萬，先據華州。

translations.literal: Wang Pi to lead ten thousand armored soldiers and seize Huazhou first.
translations.idiomatic: and Wang Pi with ten thousand armored men to seize Huazhou first.

sentences.zh: 歡若西來，王羆足得抗拒；

translations.literal: If Huan comes from the west, Wang Pi will be fully able to resist him;
translations.idiomatic: If Huan comes west, Wang Pi can hold him;

sentences.zh: 如其入洛，寇洛卽襲汾晉。

translations.literal: if he enters Luoyang, Kou Luo will at once raid Fen and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: if he pushes on to Luoyang, Kou Luo will strike Fen and Jin from behind.

sentences.zh: 吾便速駕，直赴京邑。

translations.literal: I myself will quickly drive my carriage and go straight to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: I will ride hard for the capital myself.

sentences.zh: 使其進有內顧之憂，退有被躡之勢。

translations.literal: Thus he will have worry for what lies within when advancing, and the momentum of being trampled when retreating.
translations.idiomatic: He will advance with trouble at his back and retreat with us on his heels.

sentences.zh: 一舉大定，此為上策。

translations.literal: One stroke and the great settlement—this is the upper strategy."
translations.idiomatic: One move settles everything. That is the best plan."

sentences.zh: 」衆咸稱善。

translations.literal: All praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed it was sound.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，太祖帥衆發自高平，前軍至於弘農。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the Grand Duke led the host setting out from Gaoping; the vanguard reached Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Grand Duke marched from Gaoping; the vanguard reached Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 而齊神武稍逼京邑，魏帝親總六軍，屯於河橋，令左衛元斌之、領軍斛斯椿鎮武牢，遣使告太祖。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Qi Shenwu gradually pressed the capital. The Wei emperor personally commanded the Six Armies and encamped at Heqiao, ordering Left Guard Yuan Binzhi and Camp Commander Hus Chun to garrison Wulao, and sent envoys to inform the Grand Duke.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shenwu was meanwhile closing on the capital. The Wei emperor took the field in person at Heqiao, posted Yuan Binzhi and Hus Chun at Wulao, and sent word to the Grand Duke.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂左右曰：「高歡數日行八九百里，曉兵者所忌，正須乘便擊之。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke said to those at his side: "Gao Huan covers eight or nine hundred li in several days' march—that is what those skilled in warfare fear. We must seize the opportunity and strike him.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Duke told his staff, "Gao Huan is marching eight or nine hundred li in a few days—a pace any seasoned commander dreads. We should hit him while we can.

sentences.zh: 而主上以萬乘之重，不能決戰，方緣津據守。

translations.literal: Yet the Son of Heaven, bearing the weight of the imperial carriage, could not commit to decisive battle and merely held the line along the fords.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor, with the throne on his shoulders, would not fight it out and only dug in along the river crossings.

sentences.zh: 且長河萬里，扞禦為難，若一處得度，大事去矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, the long river stretches ten thousand li—defending it is hard; if he finds one crossing, the great enterprise is lost."
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River runs for thousands of li—no line holds everywhere. One breach and everything is lost."

sentences.zh: 」卽以大都督趙貴為別道行臺，自蒲阪濟，趣幷州。

translations.literal: He thereupon made Grand Governor Zhao Gui a separate-route branch secretariat, to cross from Puban and hasten toward Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Grand Governor Zhao Gui as a separate column to cross at Puban and drive on Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣大都督李賢將精騎一千赴洛陽。

translations.literal: He dispatched Grand Governor Li Xian to lead one thousand elite cavalry to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Governor Li Xian was sent with a thousand picked horsemen toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 會斌之與斛斯椿爭權不協，斌之遂棄椿還，紿帝云：「高歡兵至。」

translations.literal: Just then Binzhi and Chisi Chun were at odds over power; Binzhi abandoned Chun and fled back, deceiving the Emperor with the word "Gao Huan's troops have arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Binzhi and Chisi Chun were then feuding for power. Binzhi deserted Chun and rode back, telling the emperor falsely that Gao Huan was upon them.

sentences.zh: 七月丁未，帝遂從洛陽率輕騎入關，太祖備儀衛奉迎，謁見東陽驛。

translations.literal: On the dingwei day of the seventh month the Emperor then led light cavalry from Luoyang into the Pass; the Grand Duke prepared ceremonial guard to welcome him and received audience at Dongyang Post Station.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day in the seventh month the emperor fled Luoyang with light cavalry into the Pass. The Grand Duke met him with full ceremony at Dongyang Post Station.

sentences.zh: 太祖免冠泣涕謝曰：「臣不能式遏寇虐，遂使乘輿遷幸。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke removed his cap, weeping, and apologized: "Your servant could not check the ravages of the brigand and thus caused the imperial carriage to shift its dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Duke bared his head and wept. "I failed to hold back the rebel," he said, "and forced Your Majesty from the capital.

sentences.zh: 請拘司敗，以正刑書。

translations.literal: I beg that I be arrested under the statute of failure in office, that the law may be upheld."
translations.idiomatic: Arrest me under the law of dereliction and let justice be done."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「公之忠節，曝於朝野。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Your loyalty and integrity are manifest to court and countryside alike.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Your loyalty is plain to the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 朕以不德，負乘致寇。

translations.literal: I, lacking virtue, bore the imperial carriage and brought on the brigand.
translations.idiomatic: It was my own lack of virtue that brought the rebel down on us.

sentences.zh: 今日相見，深用厚顏。

translations.literal: To meet you today fills me with deep shame.
translations.idiomatic: To face you now shames me deeply.

sentences.zh: 責在朕躬，無勞謝也。

translations.literal: The blame rests on my person—trouble yourself with no apology."
translations.idiomatic: The fault is mine alone—do not apologize."

sentences.zh: 」乃奉帝都長安。

translations.literal: He thereupon escorted the Emperor to the capital at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He then conducted the emperor to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 披草萊，立朝廷，軍國之政，咸取太祖決焉。

translations.literal: Clearing the brush wilderness they established the court; military and state affairs all fell to the Grand Duke's decision.
translations.idiomatic: They cleared the wilds, raised a court, and put every military and civil matter in the Grand Duke's hands.

sentences.zh: 仍加授大將軍、雍州刺史，兼尚書令，進封略陽郡公，別置二尚書，隨機處分，解尚書僕射，餘如故。

translations.literal: He was further granted Grand General, Governor of Yongzhou, concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Lueyang Commandery; two Masters of Writing were separately established for discretionary disposition; he was relieved of Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; other offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand General and governor of Yongzhou, given concurrent charge of the Masters of Writing, and raised to Duke of Lueyang. Two secretaries were added for day-to-day business; the vice directorship was dropped; everything else stood as before.

sentences.zh: 太祖固讓，詔敦諭，乃

translations.literal: The Grand Duke firmly declined, but edicts repeatedly urged him, and he thereupon
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Duke refused repeatedly until imperial orders pressed him, and at last he

translations.literal: (grant)
translations.idiomatic: (grant)

translations.literal: accepted.
translations.idiomatic: accepted.

sentences.zh: 初，魏帝在洛陽，許以馮翊長公主配太祖，未及結納，而帝西遷。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Wei emperor was at Luoyang, he had promised to give Princess Chang of Fufu in marriage to the Grand Duke; before the union could be concluded the emperor shifted west.
translations.idiomatic: While the Wei emperor still held Luoyang he had promised the Grand Duke marriage to the Princess Chang of Fufu, but the court moved west before the wedding could take place.

sentences.zh: 至是，詔太祖尚之，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: At this juncture edicts directed the Grand Duke to take her in marriage and appointed him Commandant of the Riding Companion.
translations.idiomatic: Now an edict bound the marriage and made him Commandant of the Riding Companion.

sentences.zh: 八月，齊神武襲陷潼關，侵華陰。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Qi Shenwu launched a surprise attack and seized Tong Pass, invading Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Qi Shenwu stormed Tong Pass and raided Huayin.

sentences.zh: 太祖率諸軍屯霸上以待之。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke led the various armies to encamp at Bashang and await him.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Duke camped the army at Bashang to meet him.

sentences.zh: 齊神武留其將薛瑾守關而退。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu left his general Xue Jin to hold the Pass and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shenwu left Xue Jin to guard the Pass and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃進軍討瑾，虜其卒七千，還長安，進位丞相。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke thereupon advanced to attack Jin, captured seven thousand of his troops, returned to Chang'an, and was promoted to Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Duke attacked Jin, took seven thousand prisoners, returned to Chang'an, and was made Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，齊神武推魏清河王亶子善見為主，徙都於鄴，是為東魏。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter Qi Shenwu set up Shanjian, son of Prince Qinghe Yuan Dan, as ruler and moved the capital to Ye—this was Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Qi Shenwu enthroned Shanjian, son of Prince Qinghe Yuan Dan, moved the capital to Ye, and founded Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣儀同李虎與李弼、趙貴等討曹泥於靈州，虎引河灌之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he dispatched Yitong Li Hu, together with Li Bi, Zhao Gui, and others, to attack Cao Ni at Lingzhou; Hu diverted the river to flood him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he sent Yitong Li Hu with Li Bi, Zhao Gui, and others against Cao Ni at Lingzhou. Hu dammed the river to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 明年，泥降，遷其豪帥于咸陽。

translations.literal: The next year Ni surrendered, and his tribal chieftains were relocated to Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Ni surrendered and his chieftains were resettled at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 閏十二月，魏孝武帝崩。

translations.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month Emperor Xiaowu of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary twelfth month Emperor Xiaowu of Wei died.

sentences.zh: 太祖與羣公定策，尊立魏南陽王寶炬為嗣，是為文皇帝。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke, with the assembled dignitaries, settled on a plan and raised Prince Nanyang Yuan Baoju as successor—this was Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Duke and the senior officials chose Prince Nanyang Yuan Baoju as heir—the man who became Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.idiomatic: The entire chapter was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju Zhou Shu (November 1971).
